ideas.title: Carve a log, launch it, hop in
ideas.goal: The player carves a log at the water's edge with the adze (each mouse stroke knocks a chip out), sees the waterline drawn on it while they carve, slides it into the bay and hops in: their own hull floats, leans or rolls with Lumi in it. Then they pull it back and carve again. Fun because carve and test are ten seconds apart, and the boat is theirs.
ideas.toward: A made thing that keeps every cut and does what its real shape and weight would do in the water (BIG_GOAL.md), and the boat candidate's first step.
ideas.idea: The log is a voxel block (like the chip stone's): an adze stroke removes the voxels inside its blade's swept wedge, so every chip stays gone. The hull surface comes from the voxels (marching cubes); its buoyancy and righting moment are integrated from that mesh against the water surface each frame on the GPU, with Lumi's weight where it lands. Sliding in is a rigid body on the beach slope; Lumi hops in with a jump arc, not a climb. Someone watching sees chips fly, the waterline line move up the hull, and the boat settle, lean or roll with Lumi.
ideas.form: physics/hull.jl (validated on a box and a sphere), a beach plugin in Jump in, a film of two carvings: one rolls Lumi into the sea, the next one floats.

ideas.title: A clay dam the water wears
ideas.goal: The player presses clay into the stream with the beak, handful by handful, until the water banks up into a pond behind it; the water finds the thin places and wears channels into the clay, so they patch it while the pond rises. Fun because every press shows at once in the water and the water answers by carving back.
ideas.toward: A material that keeps what was done to it twice over: the player's presses and the water's wearing both stay in the clay (BIG_GOAL.md), and building that changes the island.
ideas.idea: Shallow water on the stream's own heightfield (8 x 24 m at 8 cm cells, finite volumes on Mantle, checked against the Ritter dam break). The clay is a height layer the beak adds to where it presses; it erodes where the water's bed shear stress beats the clay's critical shear (an excess-shear erosion law), so fast water over a low spot cuts a notch that deepens until it is patched. Someone watching sees the water climb, a trickle start over a low spot, the notch widen, and Lumi slap clay into it.
ideas.form: physics/shallow.jl with an erosion layer, a stream plugin in Jump in, a film of a dam that holds after two patches.

ideas.title: Sun prints of the friends
ideas.goal: The player lays a sheet of sun paper on the meadow, puts leaves, stones and things they made on it (or asks a friend to stand still on it) and lets the sun print them: every print is the real shadow the sun cast, blurred where something moved. Fun because nothing comes out the same twice, and a fidgety friend leaves a ghost.
ideas.toward: Paper that keeps what was done to it: the print records the light that actually fell on it, and the island's things made by hand become pictures that stay on the cottage wall.
ideas.idea: Cyanotype chemistry is simple and real: blueness = 1 - exp(-dose / D0), where dose is the sunlight that reached each texel of the sheet, summed over the exposure. The path tracer (Raycore rays from each texel to the sun, soft shadows from the sun's real disc, light through translucent leaves) gives the irradiance each second; objects and friends that move during the exposure leave half-dark trails. Rinsed, the sheet keeps the print for good.
ideas.form: physics/sunprint.jl (a Raycore kernel), a plugin on the meadow, a film of a print developing with Pinchy fidgeting on it, and the prints hung on the cottage wall.

ideas.title: Lay a campfire that catches
ideas.goal: The player stacks tinder, twigs and logs by hand and lights it: a well-laid fire climbs from the tinder to the logs, a packed or damp one smoulders and dies, and the next morning the half-burnt sticks show which side burned. Fun because laying a fire is a real skill with a clear answer.
ideas.toward: Things laid by hand that behave by material and arrangement, and keep the char of their burning.
ideas.idea: Each stick is a 1-D heat conduction problem through its radius with a moving char front (wood pyrolysis: a front that moves ~0.6 mm per minute once the surface passes ~300 C, releasing gas); a stick's flame height follows its heat release (Heskestad's correlation), heat goes stick to stick by radiation with view factors from the real stack, packing limits the air. Flames are a Hikari emissive volume sized from that heat release, not a colour on the sticks; the char front darkens and shrinks each stick where it burned.
ideas.form: physics/fire.jl, a plugin by the cottage, a film at dusk of one fire that catches and one that dies, and the charred sticks in the morning.
